item.title: Exponential Stability of Slow--Fast Stochastic Systems with a Small Delay
item.description: arXiv:2610.19008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the exponential stability of coupled slow--fast stochastic systems with a small delay. Under an averaged Lyapunov condition, we establish practical $p$th-moment exponential stability for $0<p<2$ using a cutoff-function approach to handle singular Lyapunov derivatives near the origin. Exponential stability in the $p$th moment and almost surely is further obtained through two distinct mechanisms: homogeneous dissipation of the fast dynamics or vanishing sensitivity of the slow coefficients to the fast state near the origin. We extend these results to locally Lipschitz systems, establishing exponential stability with arbitrarily high probability for bounded sets of initial data, thereby broadening the applicability of stability analysis for stochastic systems with delayed feedback. Numerical examples illustrate our results.
item.dc:creator: Yudong Wang, Kele Sun, Shijie Zhou, Xuerong Mao

item.title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms for Pullback Finite Element Methods on Complex Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.19092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a method for solving partial differential equations on complex domains by learning smooth, invertible mappings from a fixed reference domain using Neural Spline Flows (NSFs). Monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers ensure a strictly positive Jacobian determinant by construction, eliminating the need for Jacobian-sign penalties. A diffeomorphic pullback transfers the weak form of the PDE to the reference domain, enabling finite element analysis on reusable structured meshes. To generalize across shapes, a shared NSF is conditioned on low-dimensional latent codes learned through an auto-decoder framework; a subsequent encoder predicts these codes for unseen geometries in a single forward pass. For a given learned map, the pullback preserves the mathematical structure of the PDE and is exactly equivalent to solving on the domain represented by that map. Because the learned domain generally approximates the target geometry, geometric mapping error remains distinct from finite element discretization and quadrature errors. Numerical benchmarks show that sufficiently accurate learned mappings yield reliable finite element solutions. By avoiding repeated generation of unstructured meshes, the method addresses a bottleneck in simulation workflows. The fixed reference mesh also creates opportunities for efficient assembly, memory-aligned data access, and precomputed quadrature. The resulting framework assigns geometric complexity to the neural network while retaining conventional finite element discretization and convergence properties on the learned domain, with overall accuracy also governed by geometric fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Kalogeris, Anaksagoras Spitas, Konstantinos Atzarakis, George Stavroulakis, Vissarion Papadopoulos

item.title: Variationally correct loss functions for nonlinear parametric problems and their neural approximations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct computable a posteriori error estimators for parametric families of nonlinear elliptic problems by measuring the residual of a variational formulation in the dual norm of a closed subspace of the test space. A single abstract theorem shows that the resulting estimator is bounded above and below by the error in the trial norm, i.e., it is a variationally correct loss function. Two instances are covered. The first considers an $L_2$-like test space, yielding a nonlinear first-order system least-squares loss function that certifies arbitrary, possibly meshless, approximations. The second breaks the test space, yielding a nonlinear discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin loss function computed by element-local problems. All assumptions are verified for quasilinear diffusion, including monotone fluxes and semilinear problems, and a nonlocal Kirchhoff model. Numerical studies train neural networks approximating the parameter-to-solution maps with the latter loss and measure the ratio of loss to squared error.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cort\'es Castillo, Wolfgang Dahmen, Jay Gopalakrishnan

item.title: Solving a sequence of eigenvalue problems using snapshot and row subsampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.19326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving $A_i\vec{x}_i= \lambda_i\vec{x}_i$ where $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $N \gg 1$ and (usually) $\lambda_i$ is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of $A_i$. Often, the matrices $A_i$ come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter $p \rightarrow A(p)$, that is $A_i = A(p_i)$, so the matrices $A_i$ change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter $p$ or the matrix $A(p)$ as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Hrobat, Yuji Nakatsukasa

item.title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed as edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS), for solving the Helmholtz problem with large wavenumbers. The problem is discretized using $H^1$-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size $h$ decreasing faster than $k^{-3/2}$ such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to $k$. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, \emph{Multiscale Model. Simul.}, 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. The approximation properties of this coarse space to the discrete solutions from the primal and adjoint problems are derived by a novel conforming Galerkin finite element method based upon a nonstandard variational formulation. This work represents the first theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space at the discrete level. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.
item.dc:creator: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yueqi Wang

item.title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.
item.dc:creator: Zhengjie Sun

item.title: A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with low regularity potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.19430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. The NLSEwPP is then directly discretized by the standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral (TS-FP) method with the mesh size chosen according to the potential projection parameter, resulting in the fully discrete TS-PP-FP method. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Weizhu Bao, Qingyuan Sun, Chushan Wang

item.title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.19435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.
item.dc:creator: Xinran Bai, Yu Du, Haijun Wu

item.title: A Stabilized CR-CR Method for Fourth-Order Elliptic Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a CR-CR method for strain gradient elasticity and prove its robustness with respect to the Lame parameter $\lambda$ and the length scale $\iota$. The method introduces the strain as an independent symmetric tensor and discretizes both the strain and the displacement using CR elements. The commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator with the relevant differential operators leads the robustness with respect to $\lambda$. A stabilization term weakly imposes the relation between the strain and the symmetric gradient of the displacement. The method also applies directly to the biharmonic equation and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems. For these problems, we prove that the CR-CR method is equivalent to an RT-CR method proposed by Huang and Tang. This result extends the classical equivalence between the RT-P0 mixed method and the CR method for the Poisson equation to fourth-order problems. The equivalence shows that the stabilization term arises naturally from the RT-CR mixed formulation.
item.dc:creator: Yule Sun, Shudan Tian, Qian Zhang

item.title: Nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability of polynomial spectral Ritz projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.19531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with Laplacian on a square domain. Its norm grows proportionally to the square root of the polynomial degree, up to a cubic logarithmic factor. The upper bound uses an integral representation of the discrete gradient projection in terms of one-dimensional semigroup kernels and a rank-two Duhamel comparison between the mass-matrix semigroup and its infinite-dimensional counterpart. The lower bound follows from the endpoint concentration of the Legendre kernel. As an application, we derive gradient maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations, with spatial factors optimal up to logarithmic terms.
item.dc:creator: Yongxing Guo, Yuwen Li

item.title: What Inverse Problems Can Be Solved Using Neural Networks?
item.description: arXiv:2610.19637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relationship between classical methods for solving inverse problems and neural network methods is examined. An answer is provided to the question of what inverse problems can be solved using neural networks. The answer is that neural network algorithms can solve only conditionally well-posed problems (well-posed according to Tikhonov). The reason is that the design of standard neural network algorithms violates the well-known Bakushinsky veto from the theory of ill-posed problems. It requires that any method theoretically guaranteeing a stable solution to an ill-posed problem must depend explicitly on the error level of data. The article highlights the distinction between the concept of regularization (RA) in the theory of ill-posed problems and regularization as understood in neural network training, where Bakushinsky's veto is violated. Due to this violation, any changes to the neural network architecture, regularization during training, or training dataset augmentation cannot alter the answer specified above. It is theoretically demonstrated that an ill-posed inverse problem can be solved only by using a parametric set of neural networks that explicitly depend on the known error levels (as parameters) of data. Accordingly, as an alternative to standard neural network algorithms, \neural network based regularization algorithms (NNBRAs) are proposed to solve ill-posed inverse problems. One approach to their construction involves using a regularized dataset. Such a dataset can be generated from perturbed inverse-problem data using a specific base RA explicitly depended on the error level of the data. Test solving the simplest finite-dimensional ill-posed inverse problem demonstrate that the accuracy of the NNBRA approximate solutions is comparable to that of the base RA. At the same time, errors of conventional neural network methods may be unacceptable.
item.dc:creator: A. S. Leonov, D. V. Lukyanenko

item.title: C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.
item.dc:creator: Arbaz Khan, David Mora, Alberth Silgado, Harpal Singh

item.title: Finite Volume Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.19748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This chapter focuses on finite volume methods. The finite volume method is a discretization method that is well suited for the numerical simulation of various types (for instance, elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic) of conservation laws; it has been extensively used in several engineering fields, such as fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, or petroleum engineering. Some of the important features of the finite volume method are similar to those of the finite element method: it may be used on arbitrary geometries, using structured or unstructured meshes, and it leads to robust schemes. The finite volume method is locally conservative because it is based on a ``balance'' approach: a local balance is written on each discretization cell that is often called ``control volume;'' by the divergence formula, an integral formulation of the fluxes over the boundary of the control volume is then obtained. The fluxes on the boundary are discretized with respect to the discrete unknowns.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. L. Lions; Philippe Ciarlet. Solution of Equation in ?n (Part 3), Techniques of Scientific Computing (Part 3), 7, Elsevier; Elsevier, pp.713-1020, 2000, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, 9780444503503
item.dc:creator: Robert Eymard (LAMA), Thierry Gallou{\"e}t (LATP, I2M), Rapha{\`e}le Herbin (I2M)

item.title: Smooth periodic extensions by extrapolation and blending for FFT-based differentiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-periodic functions on closed intervals are extended into sufficiently smooth periodic functions through a continuous Hermite interpolation framework with necessary and sufficient endpoint conditions, using smooth blend-to-zero operators and short extrapolation recurrences. A matrix-free method is introduced for generating these smooth periodic extensions on the fly directly from function values at equidistant points. No precomputed continuation operator or auxiliary basis construction is required. The resulting extensions can then be used for FFT-based differentiation of non-periodic functions. Numerical tests are provided to show the effectiveness of the method, including for the highly accurate solution of a 1D linear advection equation.
item.dc:creator: Ivan M\'endez-Cruz (LMPS), Faisal Amlani (LMPS)

item.title: Stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme
item.description: arXiv:2610.19806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Among the various space interpolation operators used in high-order semi-Lagrangian schemes, the case of finite element interpolation presents a somewhat incomplete stability theory, partly due to the impossibility of applying in a standard form the framework of Von Neumann analysis, even in the constant coefficient case. In this work, the stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme is stated in the case of the constant coefficient equation on a uniform mesh, using a suitable extension of the Von Neumann technique to treat block circulant matrices.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Ferretti, Michel Mehrenberger

item.title: Second-Order Flows for Approaching Stationary Points via the SAV-E Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.19884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Second-order flows represent an emerging computational framework for approaching stationary points of variational energies, characterized by damped hyperbolic partial differential equations. In this paper, we develop a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method for this class of flows, referred to as SAV-E. The resulting scheme is linear and decoupled, and we prove unconditional modified-energy stability. We further establish subsequential convergence to stationary points for the Ginzburg-Landau and conserved Swift-Hohenberg models under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments support the analysis and demonstrate robustness and efficiency compared with representative baselines and the corresponding gradient flows.
item.dc:creator: Haifan Chen, Wei Liu, Ziqing Xie, Yifang Yuan

item.title: Spherical Perfectly Matched Layer Method for Electromagnetic Scattering Problems with Large Wave Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.19982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a spherical perfectly matched layer (PML) method for the time-harmonic Maxwell scattering problem with large wavenumber. Using vector spherical harmonics and a modal transformation for the coupled transverse magnetic components, we establish the sharp wavenumber-explicit stability estimate for the truncated PML problem and prove that its inf-sup constant is of order $O(\kappa^{-1})$. We then analyze the first-order N\'ed\'elec edge element method and its continuous interior penalty counterpart. Under the condition that $\kappa^3h^2$ is sufficiently small, the preasymptotic errors in the energy norm and the $\kappa$-scaled $\mathbf{L}^2$ norm are of orders $O(\kappa h+\kappa^3h^2)$ and $O(\kappa^2h^2+\kappa^3h^2)$, respectively. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Jian Shi, Yonglin Li, Haijun Wu

item.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We approximate the solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$ of $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$ by operator networks whose only primitives are heat-semigroup functions of a fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The main result is an emulation theorem on strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--'Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$: an explicit scheme reaches $\dot H^1$-error $\varepsilon$ uniformly over coefficients with bounded carr'e du champ and bounded generator image and over $L^2$ data, with parameters depending only on the coefficient bounds, the accuracy and $K$; on the torus this gives a $C^2$-type coefficient class with constants independent of the dimension. The torus version refines this to Wiener classes of fractional regularity $A^{1+	heta}$, with an explicit rate attained by the scheme's product-defect block. The scheme unrolls the Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, controls each inexact step in the operator norm of $\dot H^1$ without Galerkin truncation, and synthesises the coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$ from the product defect of one heat layer. All parameters are explicit; the results are approximation theorems for continuum operators.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Hanrahan

item.title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present eMOOD, an entropy-guided evolution of the Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) framework for high-order finite-volume methods on unstructured meshes. A novel troubled-cell indicator based on numerical entropy production replaces the classical relaxed discrete maximum principle. Using entropy generation as a physically motivated measure of non-smoothness, the detector targets shocks, contact discontinuities and under-resolved flow features with a compact stencil. Compared with conventional MOOD detection, eMOOD reduces flagged cells by up to 75%, improving efficiency and reducing memory-access overhead. The detector is used within both the classical MOOD cascade of progressively reduced-order schemes and a novel MOOD-CWENO hybrid, which retains inexpensive linear reconstruction in smooth regions and activates nonlinear high-order reconstruction only where needed. Implemented in the open-source parallel solver UCNS3D, the methodology is assessed on the Shu-Osher shock-entropy-wave interaction, double Mach reflection, supersonic forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble interaction and triple material point problems. These benchmarks encompass strong shock interactions, shock-induced instabilities, multi-material interfaces and vortex-dominated flows, testing robustness, shock capturing and accuracy on unstructured meshes. Results show that eMOOD preserves the accuracy and robustness of reference CWENO and MOOD formulations while achieving speed-ups of up to 20% without loss of solution quality. Its compact detection stencil, reduced memory footprint and improved localisation offer a more scalable and efficient framework for massively parallel high-order compressible-flow simulations. item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Umi\'nski, Panagiotis Tsoutsanis, Ahmed A Sheikh Al-Shabab, Alan S. Dawes

item.title: Model order reduction of HDG discretizations for harmonic wave propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a projection-based model reduction method for the rapid and reliable solution of time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation problems over a frequency band, with particular emphasis on seismic applications. The high-fidelity model is based on a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization, formulated as a generalized saddle-point system coupling the volume and trace unknowns. The basis construction combines residual-based greedy sampling of the frequency parameter, enrichment with frequency derivatives of the HDG solution, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) compression. We establish the well posedness of both the high-fidelity and reduced problems and characterize their stability with inf-sup constants. We investigate the interaction between static condensation, inherent to the HDG discretization, and projection onto the reduced spaces, characterizing its implications for the reduced formulation and approximation errors. Since these operations do not commute in general, we derive a priori error estimates for both the trace and volume variables to quantify the gap between the two operations. We further identify a lifting condition on the volume reduced space that eliminates these gaps and yields a trace error estimate independent of the volume approximation error. Numerical experiments on the two-dimensional Marmousi model and a three-dimensional heterogeneous medium, with more than $10^{7}$ unknowns, illustrate the theoretical estimates and show that the reduced model achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude compared to the high-fidelity solver.
item.dc:creator: H\'el\`ene Barucq, Florian Faucher, Ha Pham, Ishak Tifouti

item.title: Fast spectral methods for Volterra integral equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop novel methods for the fast construction of spectral approximations to smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra integral operators and for the fast evaluation of smooth nonlinear Volterra integrals. The proposed methods employ the Duffy mapping, which transforms the original indefinite integral into a definite integral and maps the original causal triangular domain to a square, thereby avoiding any artificial extension of the kernel function. For smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra operators, the resulting approximations are almost-banded and lower-banded, respectively. The $N\times N$ principal finite section of these approximations can be constructed in $O(N)$ and $O(N^2)$ flops, respectively, via recurrence relations. For Volterra integrals with a smooth kernel that depends nonlinearly on a given function, recurrence relations lead to fast evaluation with a complexity of $O(N^2\log N)$ when the function is approximated by a degree-$N$ Chebyshev approximant. These spectral approximations and evaluation procedures give rise to fast and stable spectral methods for solving Volterra integral equations, as well as a broad class of problems involving Volterra integral operators. Extensive numerical experiments show that these spectral methods significantly outperform existing methods in terms of stability, speed, accuracy, and ease of implementation.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Kuan Xu

item.title: Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Mat\'ern DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Mat\'ern kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Oskar Broukal, Michael Feischl, Conor Osborne

item.title: Scaled Companion Linearizations for Coefficientwise Backward Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.20285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central goal in solving a polynomial eigenvalue problem is to compute eigenpairs that are exact for a nearby polynomial, with each coefficient perturbation bounded by a modest multiple of unit roundoff times that coefficient's norm. A backward stable eigensolver for a linearization does not automatically provide this coefficientwise relative guarantee. Scaling can improve accuracy, but a single scaling may not work across a widely spread spectrum. We construct a family of scaled companion linearizations that covers the nonzero complex plane. Each linearization is paired with a region and an eigenvector recovery rule for which the backward-error amplification factor is bounded at exact pencil eigenvectors, independently of coefficient norm disparities. Tropical roots guide the construction, and their multiplicities reduce the number of required solves. These results provide a basis for coefficientwise relative backward stability across the spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Javier P\'erez

item.title: Generalization of Strang-Fix remark for discrete maximum principles on tetrahedral meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most of qualitative properties of finite element (FE) approximations for various PDE models, in particular the validity of the discrete maximum principles (DMPs), are usually guaranteed by certain geometric properties (e.g. acuteness/nonobtuseness) of FE meshes used. In this work, we revisit the linear FE discretization of the Poisson equation and discuss, in the context of DMPs, the representation of the stiffness matrix entries in terms of the edge lengths and cotangents of the dihedral angles of the tetrahedral meshes, thus avoiding the common use of face areas and element volumes. Using this type of entry representation, certain structural properties of meshes, and simple trigonometric relations, as proposed in the two-dimensional case by Strang and Fix, we show that DMPs still hold (as the stiffness matrices remain $M$-matrices) for many tetrahedral configurations with obtuse dihedral angles. Such a relaxation of the standard acuteness/nonobtuseness conditions can be vital in practical calculations, as these angle properties are difficult to preserve in global and local mesh refinements. Several representative examples are presented.
item.dc:creator: Safdar Ali, Maksat Ashyraliyev, Sergey Korotov, Sergei Silvestrov

item.title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT
item.description: arXiv:2610.19043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Because its binary optimization landscape contains exponentially many local optima, MAX-CUT is highly sensitive to initialization. We study Particle Polynomial Relaxation (PPR), a moment-based nonconvex continuous reformulation possessing an advantageous optimization landscape. We warm-start PPR with Combinatorial Multigrid (CMG), a spectral graph-coarsening method that produces structure-aware initial solutions in near-linear time without training data. On \texttt{t2g20} ($n=400$), benchmark instance with known exact optimum, the combined CMG+PPR pipeline reaches $97.5\%$ of optimum on average and $98.4\%$ on the best run. An extended variant with discrete local-search refinement reaches the published optimum on all sixty Biq Mac instances evaluated by a recent neural branch-and-bound method. Using a sparse CSR representation, the same approach scales to G-set instances with up to $20{,}000$ vertices reducing memory requirements by up to $3333\times$ while maintaining a consistent improvement over the CMG warm start. Gains are largest on sparse weighted graphs; on dense graphs we complement the pipeline with spectral sparsification.
item.dc:creator: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Harris Teague, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard Lethin, Chris Lott, Roland Memisevic, Fatih Porikli

item.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme I: discrete orthogonal basis construction and expansion on velocity space
item.description: arXiv:2610.19486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Velocity space discretization is a primary source of computational cost in deterministic methods for multiscale gas flows. A fixed velocity grid often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom (DOFs), particularly under near equilibrium conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a nonequilibrium-capturing formulation based on the unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS), in which the number of kinetic DOFs adapts locally to the degree of nonequilibrium. A discrete orthogonal basis is constructed for numerical implementation, and the velocity distribution function is decomposed into an analytical local equilibrium and a basis expanded nonequilibrium component. The retained, locally adapted DOFs are evolved directly, substantially lowering computational overhead while preserving the discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as accurately capturing nonequilibrium states. The formulation retains the core multiscale coupling of molecular transport and collision inherent to UGKS, providing explicit and implicit schemes for unsteady and steady flows, respectively. Numerical tests across a wide range of flow speeds and rarefaction regimes (from continuum to highly rarefied) demonstrate close agreement with benchmark solutions. For unsteady flows, the explicit scheme achieves speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 over the standard UGKS. In steady state tests, only about $2\%$ of the original kinetic DOFs are required in continuum regions, accelerating each implicit iteration by a factor of 33.87. Even in the most rarefied cases, the scheme captures nonequilibrium behavior using only about $27\%$ of the original DOFs.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Liu, Kun Xu

item.title: An unconditionally convergent discontinuous Galerkin neural network method activated by plane waves for Helmholtz equation and Maxwell's equations
item.description: arXiv:2506.09309v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we propose a discontinuous Galerkin plane wave neural network (DGPWNN) method for approximately solving Helmholtz equation and Maxwell's equations. In this method, we define an elliptic-type variational problem as in the plane wave least square method with $h-$refinement and introduce the adaptive construction of recursively augmented discontinuous Galerkin subspaces whose basis functions are realizations of element-wise neural network functions with hp-refinement, where the activation function is chosen as a complex-valued exponential function like the plane wave function. A sequence of basis functions approaching the unit residuals are recursively generated by iteratively solving quasi-maximization problems associated with the underlying residual functionals and the intersection of the closed unit ball and discontinuous plane wave neural network spaces. The convergence results of the DGPWNN method are unconditional only if nonlinear initial parameters for the quasi-maximizers are selected by suitably distributed propagation directions, and established without the assumption on the boundedness of the neural network parameters. Numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Long Yuan, Menghui Wu, Xiaoqiang Yue

item.title: On the optimization of discrepancy measures
item.description: arXiv:2508.04926v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerical optimizations can find point sets with lower discrepancies than prior methods based on algebra, and $L_2$ discrepancies are computationally attractive for this. The $L_2$ star discrepancy unreasonably emphasizes the origin and Matou\v{s}ek pointed to a serious drawback. He showed that the $L_2$ star discrepancy of $n$ points at $(1,\dots,1)\in[0,1]^d$ is less than the root mean squared $L_2$ star discrepancy of $n$ random points until $n>(3/2)^d-1$. We introduce the \emph{average squared discrepancy} (ASD) which averages $2^d$ versions of the squared $L_2$ star discrepancy, one for each vertex of $[0,1]^d$. We show that it can be computed in $O(dn^2)$ work and that it does not suffer from Matou\v{s}ek's repeated-point pathology. We inspect several $L_2$ discrepancies that do not favor the origin over other vertices. Only two of them avoid the repeated-point pathology: a symmetric discrepancy and a periodic discrepancy. The symmetric discrepancy has a twin-point pathology where point sets with only $2$ distinct points can be better than random points until $n\ge 3^d$. We also study weighted $L_2$ discrepancies introduced by Hickernell that use some product weights. Weighting lower dimensional projections reduces but does not eliminate the repeated-point pathologies. A range of numerical experiments showcase recent progress in the construction of sets with low $L_2$ discrepancies for many different measures. In our examples, optimizing the ASD also gives good results for \emph{the other} discrepancies we consider, especially in lower dimensions. This version corrects some of the threshold sample sizes n at which random points become better than n repeated points for some discrepancy measures. In particular, the periodic L_2 discrepancy has no repeated point pathology.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Cl\'ement, Nathan Kirk, Art B. Owen, T. Konstantin Rusch

item.title: Accelerated decomposition of bistochastic kernel matrices by low rank approximation
item.description: arXiv:2510.26574v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an accelerated algorithm for the approximate eigenvalue decomposition of symmetrically normalized kernel matrices, focusing on a bistochastic normalization. Our approach constructs a low rank approximation of the original kernel matrix by the pivoted partial Cholesky algorithm, and uses it to compute an approximate decomposition of its normalization without requiring the formation of the full kernel matrix. The cost of the proposed algorithm depends linearly on the size of the employed training dataset and quadratically on the rank of the low rank approximation, offering a significant cost reduction compared to the naive approach. We derive trace norm error bounds for the approximation of two classes of normalized kernel matrices. We apply the proposed algorithm to the kernel based extraction of spatiotemporal patterns from chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamics, using a distributed GPU implementation that can scale to large datasets.
item.dc:creator: Chris Vales, Dimitrios Giannakis

item.title: Stochastic Multigrid Method for Blind Ptychography
item.description: arXiv:2511.01793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Blind ptychography reconstructs an object and a probe from diffraction measurements collected over overlapping scan regions. We introduce a reconstruction framework with two complementary operations. Local coordination adjusts the object and probe updates together at each scan position to account for their combined effect. Minibatch synthesis combines updates from a group of scan positions into common object and probe estimates. We provide a mathematical analysis of how these operations interact and incorporate coarse-grid corrections to refine the object at multiple spatial scales. In simulations spanning different scan overlaps and Poisson noise levels, the resulting stochastic multigrid method achieves the lowest final object and probe reconstruction errors among the compared methods in every tested case. Reconstructions of experimental test-pattern and integrated-circuit data demonstrate the method's practical applicability.
item.dc:creator: Borong Zhang, Junjing Deng, Yi Jiang, Zichao Wendy Di

item.title: Obstacle Mean Curvature Flow: Efficient Approximation and Convergence Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2512.16668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a simple and efficient numerical method to compute mean curvature flow with obstacles. The method augments the Merrimam-Bence-Osher scheme with a pointwise update that enforces the constraint and therefore retains the computational complexity of the original scheme. Remarkably, this naive scheme inherits both crucial structural properties of obstacle mean curvature flow: a geometric comparison principle and a minimizing movements interpretation. The latter immediately implies the unconditional stability of the scheme. Based on the comparison principle we prove the convergence of the scheme to the viscosity solution of obstacle mean curvature flow. Moreover, using the minimizing movements interpretation, we show convergence of a spatially discrete model. Finally, we present numerical experiments for a physical model that inspired this work.
item.dc:creator: Fabius Kr\"amer, Tim Laux

item.title: A Thermo-Kinematic Operator Splitting Framework for Stefan Problems Based on Extreme Learning Machines
item.description: arXiv:2601.16655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solving Stefan problems via neural networks is challenging because of the nonlinear coupling between the solution and the free boundary, which generally leads to a non-convex optimization problem when they are parameterized and optimized simultaneously. To address this difficulty, we propose a thermo-kinematic operator splitting framework based on Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) to decouple the solution reconstruction from the free boundary evolution. Both the solution and the complete free-boundary trajectory are represented over the full space-time domain. At each outer iteration, the solution is computed on the space-time subdomains determined by the current free-boundary trajectory, after which the interface geometry is updated through the corresponding free-boundary conditions using the computed heat fluxes. For the models considered here, each split subproblem is linear in the unknown coefficients when the required geometric quantities are held fixed. Both steps are therefore formulated as convex linear least-squares problems. The proposed framework thus avoids direct minimization of the monolithic non-convex residual functional by isolating the nonlinear solution free-boundary coupling in a reduced relaxed fixed-point iteration for the complete free-boundary trajectory. For a fixed discretization, the analysis establishes local linear convergence of the free-boundary trajectory iteration under the stated assumptions and with suitable relaxation. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions verify the accuracy of the proposed framework on benchmark problems and illustrate its applicability to physically motivated Stefan problems.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Lang, Zhiyue Zhang

item.title: Domain decomposition dynamical low-rank for multi-dimensional radiative transfer equations
item.description: arXiv:2602.14854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a domain decomposition dynamical low-rank method to solve high-dimensional radiative transfer problems and similar kinetic equations. The algorithm uses a separate low-rank approximation on each spatial subdomain, which means that, for a given accuracy, we can often use a smaller overall rank compared to classic dynamical low-rank methods. In particular, we can solve problems with point sources efficiently, that for classic algorithms require almost full rank. Our algorithm only transfers boundary data between subdomains and is thus very attractive for distributed memory parallelization, where classic dynamical low-rank algorithms suffer from global data dependency. We demonstrate the efficiency of our algorithm by a number of challenging test examples that have both very optical thin and thick regions.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Brunner, Lukas Einkemmer, Terry Haut

item.title: Efficient Thermo-Viscoplastic Analysis Using a Multi-Level hp-Finite Cell Method with Non-Negative Moment Fitting
item.description: arXiv:2604.15921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An extension of the multi-level hp Finite Cell Method is proposed for the simulation of thermoviscoplastic problems with temperature-dependent material behavior. The approach combines hierarchical adaptive refinement with a non-negative moment fitting (NNMF) quadrature scheme for efficient and robust integration of non-linear, history-dependent constitutive models on cut cells. The NNMF formulation yields sparse, positive quadrature rules that significantly reduce the number of integration points while maintaining stability and accuracy. An error-indicator-driven hp-refinement strategy enables localized resolution of strain and thermal gradients during the non-linear solution process. The framework is implemented within a partitioned thermo-mechanical scheme and evaluated on benchmark and application-oriented examples. The results demonstrate improved accuracy and substantial computational savings compared to standard integration approaches.
item.dc:creator: Jan Niklas Schm\"ake, Oliver Wege, Martin Ruess

item.title: Dynamical Low-Rank Filters for Data Assimilation
item.description: arXiv:2607.27432v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose dynamical low-rank (DLRA) filters for data-assimilation problems based on stochastic differential equations (SDEs). We first consider a Kalman filter applied to a Euler-Maruyama discretization of the SDE and observation processes, and derive a DLRA Kalman-type filter, named DLRA-JMCO, by minimizing jointly the error on the mean and covariance. We then obtain a time continuous DLRA-JMCO filter as the continuous limit of the time discrete one, and introduce a corresponding particle approximation. We also propose a strategy to enrich the DLRA-JMCO filter with a simple Gaussian process to capture the neglected dynamics in the orthogonal to the DLRA subspace. This correcting term allows the DLRA subspace evolution to be directly influenced by the observation operator. We finally propose a particle filter version of the DLRA-JMCO filter. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the proposed filters.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihito Kazashi, Youssef Marzouk, Fabio Nobile, Fabio Zoccolan

item.title: Projection geometry and relaxed quasi-orthogonality for inf-sup stable Galerkin methods
item.description: arXiv:2609.16265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an elementary, coordinate-free proof that uniformly inf-sup stable nested Petrov-Galerkin methods on Hilbert spaces satisfy relaxed general quasi-orthogonality. More precisely, for any window of $N$ consecutive levels, the sum of squared Galerkin increments is bounded by the squared error at the beginning of the window times $N^\sigma$, where $\sigma<1$. The exponent $\sigma$ and the prefactor can be chosen explicitly in terms of the uniform projection bound. The proof uses Hilbert-space projection estimates, dyadic iteration, and duality, without relying on matrix factorizations. As a corollary, we obtain explicit growth bounds for finite block-LU factors. In the symmetric indefinite case, the positive and negative spectral splittings of the Galerkin detail spaces yield a characterization of full quasi-orthogonality in terms of uniform boundedness of the associated finite-window sign operators. We also construct a self-adjoint involution and a nested, uniformly inf-sup stable Galerkin sequence for which full general quasi-orthogonality fails. For every $0<\alpha<1$, the construction yields a hierarchy whose finite-window constants have growth of exact order $N^\alpha$, along with an explicit target whose Galerkin increments are not square summable.
item.dc:creator: Tsogtgerel Gantumur

item.title: Numerical Methods for Dynamical Low-Rank Approximations of Stochastic Differential Equations -- Part II: Stochastic discretization
item.description: arXiv:2609.20317v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is the follow up (Part II) of arXiv:2601.21428, which proposed and analyzed time discretization schemes for the Dynamical Low-Rank Approximation (DLRA) of high-dimensional systems of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs). In this work, we discuss and analyze the corresponding stochastic discretization. Specifically, we consider Monte Carlo type methods to approximate the stochastic space and all related quantities of interest, leading to produce noisy interacting particle systems whose error analysis is non standard. Assuming subgaussian tails of the initial condition, in the case of elliptic diffusion, we provide convergence results for the Monte Carlo approximation of the DLR-PS-SDE integrator presented in Part I. The latter requires inversion of the Gram matrix associated to the stochastic modes. When the corresponding empirical Gramian in the Monte Carlo approximation remains full rank over the evolution, we prove a convergence rate close to the usual Monte Carlo one, i.e. $O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{M}})$, where $M$ is the sample size. If a regularization of this matrix is employed at each time-step, the rate is close to $O(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{M}})$. We also investigate intermediate options where the regularization is activated only when the smallest eigenvalue of the empirical covariance falls below a prescribed tolerance, showing convergence rates in between the one mentioned above.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihito Kazashi, Fabio Nobile, Fabio Zoccolan

item.title: A Domain Derivative for Electromagnetic Scattering by Perfect Conductors in the Time Domain
item.description: arXiv:2609.24822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A domain derivative for time-dependent electromagnetic scattering from perfect conductors is established. By proceeding through the Laplace domain, frequency-dependent bounds on solutions to Maxwell's equations are derived. These bounds are used both for establishing time regularity properties of the domain derivative and for proving convergence of the proposed Runge--Kutta convolution quadrature semi-discretization in time. A full convergence analysis is also carried out for pointwise evaluations of the domain derivative, when this time discretization is combined with a Galerkin method in space. Numerical experiments validate the convergence orders in time and space. Eventually, the domain derivative is applied in an iterative shape reconstruction algorithm, in which the electric near field is measured at some receiver positions away from the perfect conductor. Numerical examples show the feasibility of this algorithm and in particular highlight its robustness, when additional noise is applied to the data.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Kn\"oller

item.title: Efficient Geometry Representation Strategies for the Shape Optimization of Profile Extrusion Dies
item.description: arXiv:2609.27602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The design of profile extrusion dies remains a challenging task due to the complex rheological behavior of polymer melts and the geometric intricacies of flow channels. Traditional manual optimization approaches, which rely heavily on human experience, are inefficient and often employ unvalidated heuristics. To address these challenges, we present a deterministic and explainable framework for automatic die design based on adjoint-based shape optimization. This approach enables the computation of sensitivities that directly indicate beneficial modifications to the flow channel geometry. A major difficulty in such optimization processes lies in generating boundary-conforming meshes that evolve consistently with changing geometries. To overcome this issue, we employ non-boundary conforming geometry representation methods that eliminate the need for an explicit surface representation along physical boundaries. A dedicated reconstruction technique is developed to recover accurate sensitivity information at the virtual interface between fluid and solid regions. The proposed algorithm is demonstrated on 3D geometries with varying complexity, including realistic extrusion die flow channels. Several objective functionals relevant to industrial applications, such as flow balance at the outflow, are considered. The results highlight significant improvements in performance metrics while maintaining numerical robustness. This work showcases the potential of adjoint-based techniques for automated die design in a domain still largely governed by manual trial-and-error procedures, establishing a foundation for data-efficient, sustainable manufacturing workflows using computational rheology.
item.dc:creator: Jana Sasse, Maximilian Esser, Markus M\"ugge, Stefan Turek

item.title: A Pressure-Free Virtual Element Method for the Surface Stokes Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.39996v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a pressure-free virtual element method for the surface Stokes problem on polygonal approximations of closed surfaces of arbitrary genus. The method extends the planar VEM Stokes complex to discrete surfaces, yielding a nonconforming complex with an exactly tangential, $H(\operatorname{div})$-conforming velocity space, commuting interpolation, and the correct discrete cohomology. To obtain the weak consistency needed for optimal convergence, we introduce an edge correction that preserves the complex without adding degrees of freedom; the resulting construction reduces to the original complex in the planar setting. The virtual formulation requires no penalties, and a local divergence-preserving reconstruction provides a computable pressure-robust load. We also construct explicit macroelement representatives whose energy and load induce an alternative formulation on the VEM space, algebraically equivalent to a direct macroelement Galerkin method. The original virtual formulation and the macroelement method are stable and attain optimal first-order convergence in the broken $H^1$ norm and second-order convergence in the $L^2$ norm for the velocity. Numerical experiments illustrate these convergence rates, the role of the edge correction, and pressure robustness.
item.dc:creator: Jun Hu, Shengyang Xu, Hao Zhou

item.title: Rare Event Simulation of Quantum Error-Correcting Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2509.13678v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a practical approach for accessing the logical failure rates of quantum error-correcting (QEC) circuits under low physical (component) failure rate regimes. Standard Monte Carlo is often the de facto approach for studying the failure rates of quantum circuits. However, in the study of fault-tolerant error-correcting circuits, the ability to extend this approach to low physical failure rates is limited. In particular, the use of Monte Carlo to access circuits that are relatively large or have high correcting power becomes more difficult as we lower the input failure rates of the individual components (gates) in the circuit. For these reasons, many simulations studying the circuit model go no lower than end-to-end logical failure rates in the 10^{-6} regime. In this report, we outline an approach that borrows from earlier work by Bravyi and Vargo to the more complex circuit noise model. Earlier works studied both the capacity and phenomenological noise models, but the work is insufficient for generating similar simulations in the circuit-noise model. To the best of our knowledge, our team is the first to develop a full prescription of the rare event simulation by splitting technique for the circuit-based noise model. We have also generated promising results that are confirmed by standard Monte Carlo simulation under an accessible regime. This work shows that we can access noise in the circuit-model prescription of quantum error-correcting code to failure rates below 10^{-20} regime.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Mayer, Anand Ganti, Uzoma Onunkwo, Tzvetan Metodi, Benjamin Anker, Jacek Skryzalin

item.title: When is a System Discoverable from Data? Discovery Requires Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2511.08860v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The deep learning revolution has enabled major AI advances in physical sciences, particularly in discovering dynamical systems from observational data. Yet the reliability of learned surrogates and symbolically discovered models is often undermined by non-uniqueness: models may fit observed trajectories perfectly, but lack genuine predictive power. We show that chaos, despite its association with unpredictability, is often what makes governing equations discoverable. We prove that the classical Lorenz system is analytically discoverable and verify experimentally that for many systems out-of-domain generalization emerges precisely at chaos onset. Conservative systems, by contrast, are inherently non-discoverable from data alone. The prevalence of chaotic systems in benchmarks may have inadvertently obscured this limitation. These findings help explain why AI excels at weather forecasting, yet struggles in many engineering applications: the systems most amenable to discovery (chaotic ones) are often least amenable to control.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Shumaylov, Peter Zaika, Philipp Scholl, Gitta Kutyniok, Lior Horesh, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb

item.title: Wrong Operator or Blind Design? A Post-Training Diagnostic for Physics-Informed Coefficient Learning
item.description: arXiv:2608.16925v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physics-informed and hybrid models integrate data and physics, and read learned coefficients as physical. Yet a small prediction error guarantees neither that the postulated operator is right, nor that the design identifies the coefficient, nor that training reached its minimum. On one parabolic benchmark where a sensor aggregates several diffusion rates and the truth is known, a correct operator recovers the coefficient to machine precision. A wrong one leaves it $30\%$ off while the in-domain error is 1.36 times the noise, and drifts $27\%$ across windows. At $7\%$ noise the error falls below the noise; the coefficient stays $30\%$ off. Without the truth, a post-training coefficient diagnostic questions the trained model with three classical statistics, without oracle; the first two need no refit. Does it explain the data? Can the design resolve the named physics? Does the coefficient depend on the window? The specification test keeps its pre-registered false-alarm ceiling and rejects every replicate of both wrong operators tested; a network frozen at its minimum returns the same verdicts. Where the design is blind, a wrong operator confined to the unseen rate leaves the test mute; the design reading flags it beforehand. A network stopped short of its minimum mimics a wrong operator; an analytic second fit separates the two. The test has a notch against a missing reaction term, miscalibrates under correlated noise and loses power beyond $7\%$ noise. Each warning names its remedy (operator, experiment or training); silence certifies nothing.
item.dc:creator: Eric Fock

item.title: Quantitative Mean-Field Limits for Recent Variants of Consensus-Based Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.02901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is a robust and flexible zero-order, multi-particle class of methods devised to provide provable solutions to high-dimensional global optimization problems, including truly nonconvex and/or nonsmooth cases. The algorithmic framework is grounded in a principled trade-off between stochastic exploration of the search space and deterministic contraction toward a consensus point. This thesis is concerned with three recently established variants of CBO. The $\delta$-CBO method is similar to the classic CBO method, with the difference that the diffusion function is constant. The consensus freezing (CF) scheme can be understood as a piecewise CBO method. The overall time horizon is divided into intervals in which the consensus point is fixed. The consensus hopping (CH) scheme can be understood as a deterministic iterative scheme that jumps at each iteration to a Gaussian distribution centered at the consensus point of the previous distribution. The central contribution of this thesis is the rigorous derivation of propagation of chaos results for all three schemes. For each variant, we establish that the empirical measure of the interacting particle system converges, as the number of particles $N$ approaches infinity, to the solution of the corresponding mean-field equation. Two regimes are treated: first, on a high-probability set on which the empirical measures are uniformly bounded; second, in the unrestricted setting, where moment bounds and a careful treatment of the inter-particle dependence yield convergence without imposing conditioning on favorable events. The propagation of chaos estimates are derived by the coupling method. Together, these results provide quantitative propagation of chaos estimates for all three CBO variants and establish that the particle systems faithfully approximate the idealized mean-field dynamics in the large-particle limit.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Haug
